correctness.rationale: For odd n>=5 attaining the exact Barba bound, Barba equality yields Gram AA^T=A^TA=(n-1)I+J after compatible signed normalizations and q=sqrt(2n-1) an odd integer. A*1=q*1, so A^(-T)=(A-J/q)/(n-1), whose entries never vanish. The zero-cofactor/maximizing-fractional-entry argument forces every maximal real cube determinant basis to consist of signs, allowing all lower Auerbach bases to be represented by such inverses. For two columns, joint sign incidences N++=(n+1+2q)/4,N--=(n+1-2q)/4,N+-=N-+=(n-1)/4 give the exact all-a,b planar norm, whose three polar-zonotope determinant magnitudes are 1/4,1/4,1/(4q). Non-equality since q>=3 excludes affine regularity; Ostrovskii Thm3.1 then forces all MVSEs to be parallelepipeds. n=5 matrix J-2I and the known Brouwer–Whiteman orders establish concrete attainment, not arbitrary odd n. Independently calculated n=5 Gram and five norm pairs.
residual_risks: Conditional on actual Barba-bound attainment; cannot extrapolate to arbitrary odd orders.
Finite n=5 checker corroborates algebra, not the full quantifiers or infinite prime construction.
